stjames.boundaryReview: The bilingual primary calendar names the same Hebrew-numbered Psalm in both columns. English80:9-20 reaches the Hebrew20-verse inventory (English80 has19; Latin80 is a different Psalm). English67:2-8 uses the numbered Hebrew title followed by the blessing, beyond English67:7. English2:6-12 explicitly reaches12, whereas NABRE2 ends11. These jointly establish Hebrew/Original chapter and verse numbering, not a NABRE inheritance or an English-language assumption. Full source-native verse envelopes are converted by the pinned Hebrew-to-Standard relations; no verse text from the calendar is imported. Every one of the373 shipped Psalm appointment rows is separately pinned below to its dated primary English citation and matching Hebrew chapter; all376 English Psalm occurrences in the broader snapshot agree with their paired Hebrew chapter numerals. Three genuine printed impossible spans are retained as explicit source gaps. The profile cannot resolve an unlisted citation or substitute Latin chapter identities for these rows.

franciscan-conventual-italy.boundaryReview: The dated annual Ordo retains Roman liturgical Psalm chapter numbers: its January1 Mass hasPsalm66 with Numbers6:22-27, Galatians4:4-7 and Luke2:16-21. The official Italian Episcopal Conference publication of that same Mass identifies this asSal66(67), independently establishing the Latin/LXX chapter identity. Whole-Psalm appointments mean complete Bible chapter envelopes in this app, not an inferred responsorial refrain or cuts. Verse-specific Psalm appointments remain unavailable because their within-chapter convention is not established by this chapter review; no modern CEI wording is imported. Whole chapter families use only explicitly pinned SIL target relations, never default identity edges for unlisted source labels. Independently inspected published Martini and Brenton bodies confirm the113/114/115 and146/147 split families recorded below; in particular115 excludes all ofStandard115, and147 retains onlyStandard147:12–20.
